note: Depth decisions were derived by reading what a deep interrogation actually surfaced on this scenario. A session that settles only the core tier is correct but shallow; the depth tier is where 'grill me thoroughly' is either true or marketing.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether ad hoc runs get fresher data than the nightly batch, or both change together.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: It decides whether the fix is a per-invocation choice or a global TTL change, and the README explicitly records it as undecided.

materialDecisions.summary: How stale an ad hoc export may be before it counts as wrong.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Without a bound there is no acceptance criterion and no way to prove the fix works.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether the nightly batch may keep serving cached rows to stay inside its ten minute window.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Removing caching outright would break the nightly job; this is the constraint that shapes the whole design.
materialDecisions.repositoryHint: README.md states the ten minute window and that the 2.1.0 cache is what keeps it there.

materialDecisions.summary: Which side carries the explicit signal: a flag for the batch, a flag for ad hoc, an environment variable, or a separate subcommand.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: It changes the CLI contract that finance users share with each other, and it only has stable options once the freshness scope is settled.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether one export represents a single consistent point in time, or may mix rows read at different moments.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: The sync job rewrites the source roughly every fifteen minutes, so without a stated snapshot rule an export can silently straddle two versions of the data.

materialDecisions.summary: What an in-progress export does when the source file is rewritten underneath it.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Finishing from the initial read, restarting, and merging late rows all produce different CSVs from the same command.

materialDecisions.summary: How a stale cache entry is recognized: modification time and size, a content hash, or not caching the fresh path at all.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Timestamp checks are cheap but miss same-size rewrites that preserve mtime; hashing is exact but costs a full read on every one of the nightly batch's four hundred calls.

materialDecisions.summary: What the CLI emits when it cannot obtain data it considers valid: a non-zero exit with no CSV, the last readable rows plus a warning, or an empty CSV.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: A downstream Sheets import cannot tell a warning on stderr from success, so returning partial rows silently corrupts the very report this change exists to fix.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether a read that races the sync job is retried, and what bounds that retry.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: An unbounded retry can hang a nightly call inside a ten minute budget; no retry at all turns an ordinary sync overlap into a failed export.

forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: src/cache.js and src/exporter.js show the disk cache and its TTL.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking how often the upstream sync job rewrites the source.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: README.md and src/store.js both state roughly every fifteen minutes.

mustPreserve: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieve: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL
